newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High money rates keep Sri Lanka forex market flat.
newsitem.headline: High money rates keep Sri Lanka forex market flat.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupees traded in a narrow range early Tuesday as high call money rates prompted banks to unwind dollar positions, dealers said. At 0530 GMT the rupee was traded at around 58.46 to the dollar, near its opening level, and against the closing level of 58.42 on Monday.
"The dollar is not moving up because the money market is tight," said a foreign bank dealer. "There is a liquidity problem."
"Since money is high there's no demand for dollars," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
"Money market rates started picking up last week and people were trying to unwind their dollar positons when call rates were low," the dealer said.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar-rupee exchange rate by four and a half cents, fixing buying and selling rates at 58.2541 and 59.4309.
Call money rates stood at around 17 percent with very few lenders, dealers said.
